title: The Right Not to Be Saved

sourceEvidence.excerpt: disclosure is not automatically virtue. Initiation Before Information The modern mind has a reflexive suspicion of closed doors. We associate secrecy with conspiracy, initiation with manipulation, hierarchy with injustice, and restricted knowledge with elites protecting themselves. Often the suspicion is deserved. Priests have hidden ignorance behind sacred language. Guilds have used secrecy to keep competitors out. States classify embarrassment alongside genuine security risks. Professions cons

hook: An open door does not guarantee that everyone is ready for what lies beyond it.
